::: {.lead}
This guide helps contributors turn an idea, a run, or a finding into durable
research memory without forcing every scientific question into the same
experiment design. It keeps the evidence and the current project decision
readable, auditable, and safely separated from private run artifacts.
:::

## Result lifecycle {#result-lifecycle}

idea → planned test → evidence bundle → claim record → project decision →
reconsider, supersede, or invalidate

| Concept | What it owns | Stable reference |
|---|---|---|
| **Evidence bundle** | What executed: frozen configuration, completion count, outputs, and immutable evidence. | Evidence-of-record link. |
| **Claim record** | One condition-bound scientific conclusion. | Canonical theme page plus authored section anchor. |
| **Project decision** | What the project does now because of one or more claims. | Start Here, the owning theme's working answer, and the hub when globally relevant. |

One primary theme owns each claim. One evidence bundle may support several
linked claims when they have independently testable conclusions and decision
rules; related themes link to the canonical claim rather than copy its full
record. The canonical page plus authored section anchor is the claim identity.

## The rule in one minute {#the-rule-in-one-minute}

Static audits, compatibility probes, matched ablations, qualitative diagnostics,
and benchmarks can use different scientific designs. Each still needs a visible
question; treatment and control; panel boundary; integrity safeguards; observed
result; interpretation; evidence validity; limitations; and next decision.

::: {.callout-note title="The reporting contract"}
**Standardize the handoff, not the hypothesis.**
:::

The question decides the scientific shape. The reporting envelope makes clear
what was tested, what was observed, and what the result can support now.

## Where does this update belong? {#where-does-this-update-belong}

The theme that owns the research question is the **primary theme**. A result
with cross-theme relevance is linked from related themes, not copied into a
second current record. Dated evidence preserves provenance; the primary theme
states the readable current conclusion.

| Update | Canonical destination |
|---|---|
| Early idea | The primary theme's [Open hypotheses and ideas](experiment-ledger.{{< meta report-ext >}}#six-theme-research-map). |
| Scoped next experiment | The primary theme's [Cheapest valid next experiments](experiment-ledger.{{< meta report-ext >}}#six-theme-research-map). |
| Completed result | One primary theme's [What has been tried](experiment-ledger.{{< meta report-ext >}}#six-theme-research-map), plus sanitized dated evidence as located in the [repository map](code-map.{{< meta report-ext >}}#repository-map). Extend an existing evidence-of-record report when it already owns the result; do not force a new file for every diagnostic. |
| Cross-theme relevance | A link from the related [Research Themes](experiment-ledger.{{< meta report-ext >}}#six-theme-research-map), not a copied record. |
| Durable selected failure | The [Failure Library](failure-library.{{< meta report-ext >}}#how-to-read-the-records), only when its evidence and disclosure boundary fit. |
| Theme status or queue change | The [theme matrix and branch-complete queue](experiment-ledger.{{< meta report-ext >}}#branch-complete-next-test-queue). |
| Supersession | The primary theme and the [supersession table](experiment-ledger.{{< meta report-ext >}}#what-superseded-what); retain the historical evidence. |
| Baseline or router change | [Start Here](index.{{< meta report-ext >}}#current-recommendation), the primary theme, and the [hub status](experiment-ledger.{{< meta report-ext >}}). |
| Reusable-code boundary | The [Code Map](code-map.{{< meta report-ext >}}#code-layers), and affected code documentation when needed. |
| Correction without new evidence | Correct the owning [Research Themes record](experiment-ledger.{{< meta report-ext >}}#six-theme-research-map), mark the correction, and preserve its provenance. |
| New, split, or merged theme | Apply [When should a theme change?](#when-should-a-theme-change), then update the hub, matrix, queue, and related-theme links. |

The Qwen3-Omni neutral A2 work shows cross-theme routing: one immutable
quality-10 evidence bundle supports a Models claim about `19/20` strict
completion and promotion ineligibility, and a Native Audio claim about the
selected `3C/3P/4W` to `5C/2P/3W` semantic signal. Each theme owns the claim
whose decision changes, and the two canonical claims link directly rather than
duplicating the full experiment record.

## When should a theme change? {#when-should-a-theme-change}

Keep an idea in the nearest theme's **Open hypotheses and ideas** until all of
these conditions are true:

1. Its working answer cannot be expressed as a refinement of an existing
   theme.
2. It has an independent decision or promotion rule.
3. It needs its own evidence boundary and next-test queue.
4. It is expected to produce at least two durable claims, or it is one
   consequential multi-iteration research program.

Split a theme only when two subareas can change their working answers
independently and each has its own decision rule, evidence program, and queue.
Merge themes when those elements no longer vary independently and most new
claims require the same evidence and controls. Page length alone never creates
or splits a theme.

A new theme uses the established headings: **Current working answer**, **What
has been tried**, **What the evidence supports**, **What it does not rule out**,
**Confirmed defects, audit gaps, and uncertainties**, **Open hypotheses and
ideas**, **Cheapest valid next experiments**, and **Related themes**. Add its
hub card and matrix row, link its next work from the branch-complete queue, and
add reciprocal related-theme links. Include it in normal render, link, privacy,
accessibility, and responsive checks.

## Before the run {#before-the-run}

Write enough for a reader to understand the planned claim before outcomes can
influence it. A **falsifier** is a result that would show the proposed change
did not help under the declared condition. A **freeze** saves predictions before
expected answers or grades can influence them.

- **Why and question:** why the decision matters and the question being tested.
- **Hypothesis and falsifier:** what is expected, and the result that would not
  advance it.
- **Treatment, control, and held-fixed variables:** what changes, the matched
  comparison, and what intentionally remains the same.
- **Panel and data boundary:** composition, size, selection, and data split.
- **Material implementation details:** model and revision, prompt,
  configuration, seed, code revision, and environment when they affect
  interpretation.
- **Integrity and scoring:** label isolation, freeze, provenance, and scoring
  plan.
- **Decision rule:** the predeclared promotion, rejection, or next-step rule.
- **Operational boundary:** privacy, dataset and media rights, cost, and run
  authorization.

A field can be **not applicable** with a reason, but it may not disappear when
it affects interpretation. These are reporting questions, not a required panel
size, metric, model family, or experiment topology.

Keep private competition data, evaluation rows, credentials, raw logs, and
unapproved media out of report sources and generated outputs. Include
source-video links or limited snapshots only when the repository's recorded
rights and disclosure policy authorizes them.

## After the run {#after-the-run}

1. Preserve the smallest immutable evidence needed to audit the claim.
2. Record the **observed result** apart from the project's interpretation.
3. Assign [evidence validity](experiment-ledger.{{< meta report-ext >}}#how-to-interpret-evidence-and-decisions) and [decision disposition](experiment-ledger.{{< meta report-ext >}}#how-to-interpret-evidence-and-decisions); do not invent a parallel status system.
4. State the panel, selection, data-split, and generalization boundaries.
5. Classify a possible **confirmed defect**, **audit gap**, or **uncertainty**.
6. Say what the result rules out now and what it does not rule out.
7. Make the resulting decision and name the condition that would trigger
   reconsideration.
8. Preserve corrections and superseded claims instead of silently erasing them.

| Evidence state | Required action |
|---|---|
| **Valid but negative** | Preserve the claim and use **Not promoted under the tested condition**. |
| **Incomplete** | Preserve the evidence bundle and completion denominator; do not score it as a completed promotion comparison. |
| **Invalid** | Preserve the evidence, mark the intended claim unusable, identify affected conclusions, and require a fresh isolated run. |
| **Audit gap** | State what cannot be reconstructed without claiming an unproven defect. |
| **Corrected interpretation** | Amend the owning claim, state what changed, and preserve the earlier wording and provenance. |
| **Superseded valid claim** | Retain both claims, link `supersedes` and `superseded by`, and update current-answer surfaces when the decision changes. |

Invalid or incomplete attempts become theme claims only when their failure
changes scientific or operational understanding.

If labels, expected answers, or evaluation data may have influenced inference,
stop before making a quality claim and classify the validity problem. If
immutable evidence is missing, record an **audit gap** rather than upgrading a
result from memory. If a run is incomplete, preserve the partial observation
but do not score it as a completed promotion comparison.

The [Failure Library](failure-library.{{< meta report-ext >}}#how-to-read-the-records)
is for selected, fully disclosed development cases. It is not a place to turn
every incomplete run into a prevalence claim.

## Update the living report {#update-the-living-report}

For a completed result, add or revise one primary-theme **What has been tried**
record with these visible fields:

- Reason for testing
- Tested condition and panel
- Observed result
- Current condition-bound status
- What this rules out now
- What it does not rule out
- Possible defect, audit gap, or uncertainty
- Reconsider when
- Collapsed method, result, validity risks, and evidence

For every new or materially updated durable claim, also include:

- Canonical claim page and anchor
- Shared evidence bundle and immutable evidence link
- Evidence validity
- Decision disposition
- Decision rule and whether it was predeclared
- Gate outcome and completion denominator
- Supersedes / superseded by

A missing historical field must be reported as `not recorded`, not inferred;
it does not force a wholesale historical migration.

Keep the method, result, validity risks, and evidence in that collapsed
disclosure so the current conclusion remains scannable while audit detail stays
available.

For an upcoming test, use the established **Cheapest valid next experiments**
fields:

- Hypothesis
- Smallest valid panel or work item
- Matched controls and integrity safeguards
- Decision or promotion rule
- Boundary on what a positive result would establish

Also update [Start Here](index.{{< meta report-ext >}}) when the operational
baseline or router changes; the [theme matrix or queue](experiment-ledger.{{< meta report-ext >}}#branch-complete-next-test-queue)
when status or next work changes; the [supersession table](experiment-ledger.{{< meta report-ext >}}#what-superseded-what)
when a conclusion is replaced; the [Failure Library](failure-library.{{< meta report-ext >}})
when a durable selected failure meets its boundary; and the [Code Map](code-map.{{< meta report-ext >}})
when a reusable-code boundary changes.

## Render and verify {#render-and-verify}

QMD is editable. Its sibling Markdown and HTML report are generated outputs
and must not be hand-edited. From the repository root, regenerate all report
surfaces with:

```bash
guide_render_cache=$(mktemp -d /tmp/trecvid-guide-render.XXXXXX)
for source in docs/project-status/*.qmd; do
  page=$(basename "$source" .qmd)
  env XDG_CACHE_HOME="$guide_render_cache/cache" quarto render "$source" --to gfm --output-dir docs/project-status --output "$page.md"
done
env XDG_CACHE_HOME="$guide_render_cache/cache" quarto render docs/project-status --to html
```

Use checks proportional to the change: compare a clean isolated regeneration,
check links and authored fragments, retain the three-item navbar, inspect light
and dark desktop and phone layouts, scan outputs for private data or remote
runtime dependencies, and run `git diff --check`. Do not add scripts or CI for
this reporting workflow.

## Agent handoff {#agent-handoff}

Use this copy-and-adapt packet as guidance for a human-readable handoff. It is
not a machine schema.

```markdown
## Experiment or result name

- **Primary theme / related themes:**
- **Question / hypothesis / decision rule:**
- **Treatment / control / panel / data boundary:**
- **Revisions and immutable evidence:**
- **Canonical claim page and anchor / shared evidence bundle:**
- **Observed result / evidence validity / limits:**
- **Decision disposition / decision rule predeclared?:**
- **Gate outcome / completion denominator:**
- **Decision / reconsideration condition / supersedes / superseded by:**
- **Report pages and code paths changed:**
- **Verification:**
- **Unresolved defects / audit gaps / unknowns:**
```
